title: uae shares gain regional conflict fuels oil supply concerns 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - UAE stock markets closed higher on Friday, with Dubai outperforming its regional peer, supported by a sharp weekly rise in oil prices as ​attacks on key Middle East shipping routes fuelled concerns that supply ‌disruptions could persist.
Crude was on track to gain more than 7% for the week, while U.S. diesel prices hit a record high.
Oil flows remained restricted through the Strait of Hormuz ​as the U.S. and Iran traded attacks, while Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of ​Yemen's port of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.
Vessel ⁠transits at the Strait of Hormuz fell to seven on Thursday from 11 ​the previous day, preliminary ship-tracking data showed on Friday, well below the 10-day average ​of 15.
Brent crude, a key driver of Gulf economies, was down 3.6% at $103.75 a barrel by 1056 GMT.
Dubai's main market (.DFMGI)
, opens new tab
 advanced 0.6% after two sessions of losses, boosted by a ​4.2% surge in top lender Emirates NBD Bank (ENBD.DU)
, opens new tab
, while utility firm Emirates Central ​Cooling Systems Corporation (EMPOWER.DU)
, opens new tab
 rose 1.9%.
National Central Cooling (TABR.DU)
, opens new tab
, however, fell 2.1% after announcing the appointment of ‌Yousif ⁠Al Hammadi as its new chief executive officer.
Abu Dhabi's benchmark index (.FTFADGI)
, opens new tab
 edged up 0.03% for a fourth straight session, supported by a 3.6% rise in IHC-owned investment firm Two Point Zero Group (2POINTZERO.AD)
, opens new tab
.
State-owned energy shipping firm Adnoc Logistics & Services (ADNOCLS.AD)
, opens new tab
 climbed 2.9%, while ​energy infrastructure developer ​NMDC Group (NMDC.AD)
, opens new tab
 added ⁠3.5%.
Gains in the index were limited by a 5% decline in chemical maker Fertiglobe (FERTIGLB.AD)
, opens new tab
 and 1.5% fall in largest lender ​First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB.AD)
, opens new tab
.
Separately, the United Arab Emirates is quietly ​revising plans ⁠for a 5-gigawatt AI data center project – one of the biggest outside the U.S. – after the Iran war prompted a rethink of how and where critical infrastructure should ⁠be built, ​six people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
For ​the week, Abu Dhabi index and Dubai index recorded a weekly gain of 1.4% and 1% ​respectively, according to LSEG data.
